Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 5- to 6-day history of dry, continuous cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias, transient diarrhea; no dyspnea, chest pain, or purulent sputum.  
• Background of T2DM and hypertension (on Metformin and Lisinopril).  
• No red-flag features reported; vitals and chest exam not documented.

Working diagnosis  
Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza-like illness – most consistent with symptom cluster and time course.

Differential considerations (consistent with DDx)  
• Acute (viral) bronchitis / evolving post-viral cough – monitor if cough persists beyond 2 weeks.  
• Community-acquired (atypical) pneumonia – low-to-medium likelihood; reconsider if fever, dyspnea, or productive cough develop.  
• ACE-inhibitor (Lisinopril)–related cough – low likelihood given systemic viral features and short duration.

Management  
• Supportive care: rest, hydration, regular paracetamol for discomfort.  
• Sick leave 1–2 days; avoid workplace transmission.  
• Safety-net: return in 2–3 days if no improvement or sooner if breathlessness, fever, or chest pain; consider chest exam, vitals, and possible CXR/antibiotics at that time.  
• Chronic disease review: reinforce diabetes and BP monitoring; consider formal review with labs and vitals at next visit.  
• Alcohol: gradual reduction plan discussed (to ≤2 glasses/week, then aim for abstinence).  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discussed alcohol reduction; encouraged continued smoking cessation, balanced diet, routine exercise once recovered  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Wishes to recover from current illness and maintain control of diabetes and BP  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Eligible – T2DM and hypertension  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  None arranged today; consider diabetes educator/dietitian during GPMP  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Review in 2–3 days if no improvement; otherwise routine chronic disease review within 1 month

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection – High likelihood; matches acute onset, cough, rhinorrhea, systemic symptoms, self-limiting nature.  
2. Acute (viral) bronchitis / post-viral cough – Medium likelihood; dry cough may persist after viral prodrome.  
3. Community-acquired atypical pneumonia – Low–Medium likelihood; diabetes elevates risk, but lacks focal chest signs or dyspnea.
